answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before it can trade: creating thousands of fake agents then costs real capital, and misbehavior slashes the bond. Like a falcon that must earn its perch before hunting, an agent proves commitment first; the bond is the quartz in the foundation, hard and verifiable, while timber-built throwaway identities collapse because they cannot afford the stake. Honest agents recover their bond, attackers lose theirs.
